text:
Deadlines are a normal part of work and study, but they can feel stressful if you are not organized. The key is good time management. Start by breaking a large project into smaller tasks and giving each one its own mini-deadline. This makes the work feel less overwhelming and helps you track your progress.

Prioritization is also crucial. Not every task is equally important, so decide which ones must be finished first and focus your energy there. Sometimes, you may realize the original plan is too ambitious for the time you have. In that case, practice scope management by asking what is truly essential. Finally, never hide a problem. If you are falling behind, communicate early with your boss, teacher, or client. A simple, honest update can often lead to a new, more realistic deadline.
